pamphlet_excerpts: Cut Protection: Carving gloves woven with Kevlar or stainless steel mesh protect the holding hand.
Blood Circle: Maintain a clear arm length boundary in every direction before opening any blade.
Wound Cleaning: Wash minor carving lacerations thoroughly with mild soap and potable clean running water.
Splinter Removal: Disinfect tweezers with isopropyl alcohol before gently extracting wood fragments along entry angles.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Glove Fitting: Don a snug cut resistant glove on the hand holding the wooden block.
Step 2 - Space Clearance: Establish a complete blood circle by extending both arms outwards in full rotation.
Step 3 - Direct Pressure: Press sterile gauze firmly over minor lacerations until bleeding halts completely without oozing.
Step 4 - Sterile Dressing: Cover the cleaned wound with antiseptic ointment and an adhesive sterile fabric bandage.

B. A sharp blade lets you carve directly toward your bare thumb without wearing any protective gear.

C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
D. You should pass an open carving knife blade-first to another Scout so they can test its sharpness immediately.

pamphlet_excerpts: Pocketknife Etiquette: Close folding blades fully before passing or carrying pocketknives across the carving area.
Sheath Security: Place fixed blade knives directly into rigid protective sheaths when setting them down.
Stable Seating: Sit squarely on a sturdy chair with elbows supported near knees during cuts.
Task Lighting: Ensure bright overhead illumination reaches the carving block to track every cut path.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Card Review: Present your valid Totin Chip card showing completed edge tool safety training.
Step 2 - Bench Setup: Clear loose clutter from the bench surface and check ambient room lighting levels.
Step 3 - Posture Adjustment: Position your body securely with feet flat on floor and arms properly braced.
Step 4 - Tool Return: Close all folding knives or sheath fixed blades immediately after finishing each task.

pamphlet_excerpts: Profile Sketch: Trace front and side profile outlines onto squared basswood blocks with pencil markings.
Roughing Out: Remove waste corners rapidly using push cuts to form basic polygonal mass.
Facet Rounding: Slice faceted ridges smooth by rotating the figure under diffuse natural work lighting.
Detail Texturing: Incise eyes, hair, and clothing creases only after overall proportions stand completely balanced.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Blank Layout: Draw top, side, and front profile silhouettes squarely on all blank faces.
Step 2 - Mass Removal: Chop waste wood outside your profile lines using push cuts and stop notches.
Step 3 - Form Rounding: Shave square rectangular corners into smooth flowing curves using sweeping paring cuts.
Step 4 - Surface Detailing: Cut delicate surface textures, eyes, and feathering with a sharp detail knife.

pamphlet_excerpts: Relief Grounding: Level recessed background areas evenly using flat dogleg chisels or wide sweep gouges.
Chip Geometry: Three corner chip carving patterns require three angled incisions meeting at one point.
Pattern Transfer: Transfer geometric layouts accurately onto surfaced wood blanks using carbon tracing paper sheets.
Undercut Shadow: Undercutting perimeter edges of relief figures creates dramatic contrast against the flat background.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Board Clamping: Secure the flat carving board firmly to the benchtop using padded wooden clamps.
Step 2 - Outline Scoring: Cut vertical stop incisions along all drawn pattern outlines with a skew chisel.
Step 3 - Waste Extraction: Slice waste chips away from design borders toward scored stop cut lines cleanly.
Step 4 - Surface Leveling: Flatten the recessed background plane smoothly using a bent gouge or hand scraper.

B. By making three diagonal cuts that meet at a central point to form an inside-out pyramid
C. By burning the triangle outline with a soldering iron and sanding the middle
D. By chiseling straight down along all three sides and prying the plug out with a screwdriver
choices: A. By drilling a center hole and scraping outward with a curved gouge

C. By burning the triangle outline with a soldering iron and sanding the middle

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. By making three diagonal cuts that meet at a central point to form an inside-out pyramid
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In chip carving, a triangle is formed by making three diagonal cuts angled toward a single central bottom point, releasing a three-sided chip and leaving an inverted pyramid (p. 55).
